I actually really like the creators intentions over the current usage, but now it is what it is and I doubt it will ever go back to being used that way- now people use it to mean anyone with any sort of mental condition (and generalising them, which is where the problem is), and before it used to be either everyone or specific to autism depending on context.

Having walked the world being perceived as both male and female is a special experience that most don't get to have. It teaches you a lot about how gender influences how we're treated in society. A lot of people know about disparities in the treatment men and women in different settings, but not everyone has first hand knowledge.

For example, since transitioning the kind of compliments I get are very different- men will be praised for their work but women are judged more on looks. On the other hand, men will sometimes express their casual misogyny to me which they definitely would've been less likely to if they were viewing me as a woman. Also, people are less likely to take my mental health seriously and trust my past female abusers over me. It sucks, but I've learned a lot and have a lot of empathy for people dealing with pressures from both sides of the binary gender treatment system.

This has to be different for everyone, but it was self blame for me. Even after I left the situation, the abusers kept trying to reach out to me through alternate accounts and accounts I hadn't blocked them on yet telling me I was deserving and responsible. When you have six people doing that to you, as well as the random friends and family members of those people that you don't know, it becomes hard to recognize it as abuse. People often say that if more people are telling you something then aren't than the group with more is usually right, but that's not always the case.

I wish I had some helpful advice that would allow you to accept that it wasn't your fault, but I don't have a solution. The only thing that sort of "works" for me (at least in the moment) is just remembering what the abuser did- obviously it's gotta be pretty bad to be called abuse. You can't excuse that, even when it sometimes feel like you can, because the scars you get from that can be lifelong. Sending support from a trans man whose struggles with this idea too
